title: Analogies of the Spirit's Work and Relation
english: the Word, or so they will think according to the Scriptures. For the Trinity is not composed of something within the one divinity, nor are the spirits [called] spirits, if we do not speak of profanities, nor are men [called] gods because they are called so; for we are not in truth. If they do not realize that these things contradict: 'only the wise God' and 'alone possessing immortality,' they will not be able to be made wise by anything from the opposite of the Holy Spirit.

For these things were thus spoken by Paul, because the Word of God is the Son, and the Holy Spirit is the Spirit, and he has it inseparably according to nature, and leads into one divinity, just as it is said by those outside: 'one God from whom all things came.' Just as Paul wrote to the Romans, Galatians, and Timothy concerning the Father: 'one God' (Rom 1:25; 1 Cor 8:6), so John said concerning the Son: 'the only begotten God, who is in the bosom of the Father' (John 1:18). And concerning the Holy Spirit, Paul taught the Corinthians: 'but to another the gifts of healings in the one Spirit' (1 Cor 12:9); for the oneness of the divine and the plurality of nature are His own. And just as it was written that the Son was begotten, and the witness says: 'I came forth from the Father' (John 16:28); so it was written, and the same said: 'the Spirit of truth, which proceeds from the Father' (John 15:26), meaning it issued forth.

And just as the Son, being God and Lord, is the Son of God and Lord, so the Holy Spirit, being God and Lord, is the Spirit of God and Lord. And in the way that it is written that the Son co-exists with the Father, the same way the Holy Spirit is written 'the word of God,' and 'the spirit of his mouth,' and 'the breath of the Pantokrator' (1 Cor 15:45), because having been co-substanced, he shone forth from him; so that no one might suppose that it is something from the outside of the divinity of the Father or of his Word. For the word of the Word and the word of the mind are His own; and this is fulfilled: 'the one God and Father of all, and over all, and through all, and in all' (Eph 4:6).

And just as the Son is shown to be distinct from the Father, as it is written: 'he who has seen me has seen the Father' (John 14:9); likewise also the Holy Spirit, through which it is said: 'in this we know that God is in us, from his Spirit, which he gave us' (1 John 4:13). It is therefore necessary, since the true God is the Father, that a true God be equal to him and—

the one showing himself by his own manifestation. 5.13 And just as all things came to be through the Son, so all things were sanctified and empowered by the Spirit. For the apostles say: 'Lord, the one who made heaven and earth and the sea and all things in them; the one through the Holy Spirit, and the mouth of David your child is an icon' (Acts 4:24). And just as the Only-begotten is equal in power and similar to the Father and an authority, it is shown according to: 'Whatever the Father does, these things the Son likewise does' (John 5:19); likewise also the Spirit of God according to: 'And all these things the one and the same Spirit works' (1 Cor 12:4).

5.14 And just as regarding himself the Christ said: 'No one has known the Father except the Son' (John 16:13), so also regarding the Holy Spirit it is said similarly, that: 'No one has known the things of God except the Spirit of God.' And in the manner that the Son was called the angelic one, 'messenger of great counsel' (Rom 8:16); so also regarding the Holy Spirit, for they say: 'But we received the Spirit of God, so that we might know the things granted to us by God.' 5.15 And similar to: 'Christ the firstfruits' (1 Cor 15:20), is the saying plainly: 'and having the firstfruits of the Spirit.' And equal to: 'And the Lord to sanctify you, so that you might be sincere and blameless for the day of redemption' (Eph 4:24), is: 'so that the offering of the Gentiles may become acceptable, sanctified in the Holy Spirit.' And balanced to say: 'The one who set me apart from my mother's womb, through his grace to reveal Christ in me' (Gal 1:15), is: 'God revealed through his Spirit.'

5.16 And equal to say: 'Test yourselves, whether Christ is in you' (2 Cor 13:5), is to say: 'But we did not receive a spirit of the world, but the Spirit of God.' And equal to: 'Do you not know that you are a temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you?' (1 Cor 3:16), is that written by John: 'If we love one another, God remains in us. In this we know that we remain in him and he in us, through his own Spirit, which he gave to us' (1 John 4:13), and to: 'We shall come, I and the Father, and we will make a dwelling with him' (John 14:23). 5.17 And just as through the Father and the Son the Holy Spirit is given according to: 'I will pour out from my Spirit upon all flesh' (Joel 2:28) and according to: 'Receive the Holy Spirit' (Acts 1:8); so through the Holy Spirit the Christ, according to Paul writing to the Ephesians: 'so that he may give to you,'

title: The Identity of the Spirit with Father and Son
english: According to the wealth of his glory, [he is] to be strengthened in power through his Spirit, so that Christ may dwell in the inner man. We might have received in a similar and equal way: 'the word of the Lord came to this prophet' and 'the Lord said' and 'thus says the Lord of hosts', as that which was said by Peter in the Acts: 'it was necessary for the scripture to be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit foretold' (Acts 28:25); and that which was said by Paul to the Jews in Rome: 'the Holy Spirit spoke well through the prophet Isaiah' (Rom 15:6); and that which says: 'the Spirit says plainly' and 'thus says the Lord of hosts'.

It is also of equal value to: 'the eternal God' which was proclaimed by Paul: 'who has presented himself through an eternal Spirit' (1 Tim 6:16). And it is comparative to: 'no one is able to receive the Holy Spirit except from the Lord' and to: 'receive the Holy Spirit' and to: 'no one is able to say Jesus Christ is Lord except in the Holy Spirit' (1 Cor 12:3).

It is the same as: 'to be led by the Holy Spirit into the truth', that is, to be led by the Holy Spirit into the true faith, by being led by the Lord Christ who ordains: 'baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit' (Matt 28:19). And it is of equal strength to the one saying explicitly: 'shall we provoke the Lord? shall we be stronger than he?' (Acts 20:27) and to the writing: 'do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, in whom you were sealed for the day of redemption' (Eph 4:30). And it is analogous to: 'you shall send out your Spirit and they shall be created' and to: 'you shall send out your word, and it shall establish them'.

It is also similar to saying: 'the Lord testifies to my soul, that I do not lie' and the writing: 'the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from the Father, he will testify about me' (John 16:13); and: 'the Spirit testifies about me in the city, saying'. And it is a representation of the one saying the lordly word: 'behold, I send you as sheep in the midst of wolves' (Matt 10:16), and: 'these then, having been sent out by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia'. And it is equal to the writing: 'if you seek the testing of the Christ speaking in me', to the writing that: 'they were saying to Paul through the Spirit: do not go up to Jerusalem' (Acts 16:6). And it is kindred to: 'the Son is eternal life' which was said by him: 'the water, which I shall give' (John 4:14).

He will be in him a spring of water leaping into eternal life. This he was saying concerning the Holy Spirit, whom the believers were about to receive through him. And it is consistent with the saying, 'for we have become partakers of Christ,' which is: 'for it is impossible for those having been once enlightened and having tasted the gift, and having become partakers of the Holy Spirit.'

It is also very similar to what is said in the actions: 'tongues as of fire appeared to the apostles, dividing, and they sat upon each one, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit,' and what was said by John: 'he will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire,' which is consistent with what Moses said: 'God is a consuming fire,' and what Isaiah said: 'behold, the Lord will come like fire.' And it is consistent with the statement: 'you were circumcised by a circumcision not made with hands, in the putting off of the flesh of sins in the circumcision of Christ,' with what is written: 'circumcision of the heart in the Spirit.'

And if it is fitting to say of God the voice of Peter: 'let each one repent from his wickedness and from the evil way and let him be baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus, and he will be saved,' then for God His Spirit is likewise unchanging, and from the one who is Lord to the disciples, saying to them by name: 'receive the promise of the Father, which you heard, that John indeed baptized with water for repentance, but you shall be baptized in the Holy Spirit.' For this signifies nothing other than what his other teaching concerning enlightenment signifies, namely that the Holy Spirit performs and is able to do the same things, which is the name of the Father and of His Son, as they possess the same divinity.

The preaching of the Son and of the Holy Spirit is also unchanging and equally valid, as Paul writes to the Romans: 'for if indeed the one coming preaches another Jesus whom we did not preach, or if you receive a different spirit, which you did not receive.' The same evidence is found in: 'for I do not dare to speak anything that Christ has not accomplished through me for the obedience of the Gentiles, in word and work, in the power of signs and wonders, in the power of the Spirit of God,' with: 'the Father who remains in me, He himself does the works. Believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me.' For observe that just as it is with the Father, so also the...

title: The Word of God and the Nature of the Spirit
english: His Spirit remains with the Christ, being inseparable from the divine nature; and the divine works are done in agreement by the ineffable Trinity; and just as the Father, being in his own subsistence, is represented in the Only-begotten because of the unchangeable nature of the deity, that is, the essence; so too the Only-begotten is in the same manner in the one Holy Spirit.

And how many other things are brought forward concerning the divine Spirit that do not differ from what is written concerning God and the Father and his Only-begotten Son, from which some are contained in different places of this book, through which the course of the Logos came. 5.27 Since they will not yet say, having been questioned, that Eve is from Adam and the children from her; and how some were written as born, but she was neither a child of him, nor a sister of those born from oblivion; when it is not possible to show the unity and incomparable nature from a parable of creatures, the unseen remaining to the mind, but being endured by hearing and words. Even if a small thing, like a shadow of a likeness, should be found, one must flee from the more abundant, leaving the one who drives downward. For in no way can the example be one of identity; but it is only safe to say those things which the Scriptures have taught us according to our measures. 5.28 That therefore to be one and only Spirit of God the Father has been written, because it is separated in nature from the other spirits, but is joined to the Father and to his Son the Word of the essence; Paul is directed as writing to the Corinthians in the first epistle: 'but different gifts of healings in the one Spirit' (1 Cor 12:4); and again: 'but all these works the one and the same Spirit performs, dividing to each one individually as he wills' (1 Cor 12:11); and again: 'we were all made to drink of one Spirit' (1 Cor 12:13); and to the Ephesians: 'that through him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father' (Eph 2:18); and again: 'endeavoring to keep the unity of the Spirit' (Eph 4:3); that is: to make much guarding so that it does not divide itself from the highest unity and self-sufficient essence. 5.29 That they are also called a word, they testify thus: Paul, writing to the Ephesians: 'having taken up the armor of God and the breastplate of righteousness and the shield of faith and the helmet of salvation and the ma-'

rejoicing in the Spirit, which is the word of God. Of which a certain sword Matthew also mentioned from the person of Christ, saying: 'I did not come to cast peace, but a sword' (Matt 10:34). Not a sword, he says, but the unsearchable wisdom of the Holy Spirit, which lies beyond the peace of the sanctified hearts. And toward the Hebrews: 'for he carries all things by the word of his power' (Heb 1:3). By what kind of word? David prophesied: 'By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and by the spirit of his mouth all their strength' (Ps 33:6). And again Paul: 'for it is impossible for those having been once enlightened, having tasted the heavenly gift, and having become partakers of the Holy Spirit, and having tasted the good word of God' (Heb 6:4-5). Peter also: 'because all flesh is as grass, and all its glory as the flower of grass; the grass withered and the flower fell, and its beauty perished; but the word of God remains forever' (1 Pet 1:24). In the same manner concerning the Son, he sings in the Psalms: 'Forever, Lord, your word remains in heaven' (Ps 89:37). For many things regarding the most supreme and most divine Hypostases are handed down most mystically.

Regarding all that is proper to the Divinity, testimony is given concerning the Holy Spirit thus: Then therefore they testify concerning the pure and ineffable nature of the Holy Spirit, just as concerning God who exercises authority over all, and Father, and the Son who is over all and Lord of all, because he does not have heterousia, nor is he lesser in power and glory. And nothing of these is found to exist of itself from nothing to any creature. For what he does have, he has through the zeal of the Triad in one Divinity; and each has always been such that it is possible to know from what it is, what it is and what it is not, whether it be God or a creature. For example: that it is not a creature first, according to the heretics, but God; for the first creature turns out to be Satan. Creation has being, but is not the beginning. And this was shown in Job, and what kind of thing it is in logical terms: first, a poem. For he says the devil is one who deceives nature in manner. And that the Holy Spirit is a creature, as 'the breath of the Pantokrator,' or that he is entirely a beginning, has not been written at all. For a creation could not pre-exist the creative Spirit, and such a thing...
